item.title: Trump Directed Use of Taxpayer Money for Ads Praising His Presidency
item.description: The government-funded ads show just how much President Trump has been able to use federal money for his own aims.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Haberman, Hamed Aleaziz, Shane Goldmacher and Jonathan Swan
item.media:description: An ad that was approved by President Trump and paid for by U.S. Customs and Border Protection.

item.title: National Science Foundation Diverted $1.4 Billion in Science Funds Mandated by Congress
item.description: The move, affecting about one-fifth of the National Science Foundation’s primary research budget, is the latest sign of how the White House is asserting more control over grants.
item.dc:creator: Adam Sella, Christopher Flavelle and Irena Hwang
item.media:description: Some National Science Foundation divisions pulled back research proposals in order to comply with White House guidance to carry over funds.

item.title: Judge Blocks Border Wall Construction in Big Bend in Texas
item.description: The ruling dealt a setback to the Trump administration’s plans for hundreds of miles of barriers that have drawn local opposition.
item.dc:creator: J. David Goodman
item.media:description: A construction site for a border wall near Santa Elena Canyon in Big Bend National Park in August.

item.title: Man Accused of Sex Assault Seeks to Expunge Cornell’s Finding of Related Violation
item.description: A panel found the man responsible for attempted sexual exploitation, barred him from contact with the woman and required him to take a class and write a paper.
item.dc:creator: Maia Coleman
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Chi Phi fraternity house at Cornell University in Ithaca, N.Y., this week. Seven of the fraternity’s members have been accused of sexual assault by a fellow student.

item.title: How The New York Times Is Reporting on the Cornell Rape Investigation
item.description: Times editors explore the thinking behind our coverage of the explosive allegations that have roiled a campus and the country.
item.dc:creator: Megan DiTrolio, Mike Abrams, Nikita Stewart, Sarah Garland and Susan Wessling
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Sexual assault allegations have rocked Cornell’s campus and put the university under a spotlight.

item.title: How FlyDubai Passengers and Crew Averted Disaster After Pilot Was Stabbed During Flight
item.description: A badly wounded Indian pilot managed to unlock the cockpit door. Four Israeli men teamed up to overwhelm an attacker and avert disaster.
item.dc:creator: David M. Halbfinger, Natan Odenheimer, Adam Rasgon, Johnatan Reiss and Aaron Boxerman
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: A FlyDubai plane carrying Israeli passengers who had earlier been aboard another FlyDubai aircraft that made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia approaches Ben Gurion International Airport near Tel Aviv on Wednesday.

item.title: Indian Pilot Stabbed on FlyDubai Flight Recalls Sudden Attack
item.description: Capt. Smit Machchhar, who was stabbed by his co-pilot midair between Dubai and Tel Aviv, said he “had to act” to prevent a crash despite serious injuries.
item.dc:creator: Pragati K.B.
item.media:credit: Israel's Foreign Ministry, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Capt. Smit Machchhar in a photo released by Israel’s Foreign Ministry.

item.title: Airlines Set to Bring Israelis Back From U.A.E. After FlyDubai Cockpit Attack
item.description: The attack, on a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, halted the only direct service between the two cities since the war in Iran disrupted air traffic.
item.dc:creator: Johnatan Reiss
item.media:description: Israeli carriers in Cyprus in 2025. Two Israeli airlines, Israir and Arkia, said Friday that they had obtained “the required permissions” to land at Dubai’s airport.

item.title: Why Were 4 Pilots Aboard FlyDubai Flight 1073?
item.description: After the co-pilot stabbed the captain, two pilots who were seated in the cabin intervened alongside passengers and safely landed the Boeing 737 in Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: Karla Adam
item.media:description: A FlyDubai plane carried passengers to Tel Aviv on Wednesday after a midair cockpit attack on their earlier flight. Two other pilots who were seated in the cabin safely landed that plane.

item.title: Christa Pike Unconscious and on Ventilator After Execution Attempt
item.description: Her condition raises questions about whether Tennessee could attempt to execute her again if she is incapable of understanding what is happening.
item.dc:creator: Emily Cochrane
item.media:credit: Denny Simmons/The Tennessean/USA TODAY NETWORK, via Reuters
item.media:description: Friday’s disclosure was the most detailed information about Christa Pike’s health since she survived two rounds of pentobarbital Wednesday evening.

item.title: U.S. and Allies Agree to Release Diesel Reserves as Prices Soar
item.description: The Group of 7, which includes Britain, France and Japan, announced the release of 100 million barrels over four months, effective immediately.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Friedman and Rebecca F. Elliott
item.media:credit: Hilary Swift for The New York Times
item.media:description: The release of diesel and crude oil is designed to “stabilize immediate energy supplies,” the Group of 7 countries said in an announcement.

item.title: Sales of Hulking Pickups and S.U.V.s Sag as Fuel Prices Soar
item.description: Sales of big pickup trucks and sport utility vehicles have dipped as more Americans buy hybrids and smaller cars.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ewing
item.category: Sports Utility Vehicles and Light Trucks
item.media:description: Sales of the Chevrolet Silverado were up, but the growth came from a light-duty version of the truck. Sales of heavy-duty Silverados slumped as Americans shift away from full-size pickups and S.U.V.s.

item.title: Republicans Pull Money From North Carolina Senate Race As Midterm Prospects Dim
item.description: As the Republicans try to hold their majority, the Senate Leadership Fund is diverting resources to Kansas, which has become a growing concern for the party.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher and Theodore Schleifer
item.media:description: Michael Whatley, the Republican candidate for Senate in North Carolina, has consistently trailed his Democratic opponent in the polls.

item.title: AIPAC Is Spending Millions to Elect Friends. It’s Also Making Enemies.
item.description: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee has increasingly become a campaign issue unto itself. Some candidates have worn opposition from AIPAC as a badge of honor or made a point of rejecting the group’s support.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Medina, Theodore Schleifer, Ellen Gabler and Yair Rosenberg
item.media:description: Preparing for an AIPAC policy conference in Washington.

item.title: Flurry of Lawsuits Shows Both Parties Preparing for Post-Election Challenges
item.description: Republicans are using the courts to hunt for noncitizen voters. Democrats worry the G.O.P. is trying make it harder for eligible voters to cast ballots — and paving the way to try to toss valid election results.
item.dc:creator: Richard Fausset
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: A voter casting a ballot at Miller Elementary School in Dearborn, Mich., during the state’s primary in August. Scores of lawsuits from the two major political parties and their allies reveal the likely battle lines for post-election challenges.

item.title: California Sues to Block Trump From Weakening Fuel Economy Rules
item.description: The lawsuit is the 97th the state has filed against the Trump administration over the past year and a half.
item.dc:creator: Brad Plumer
item.media:credit: Stella Kalinina for The New York Times
item.media:description: Traffic in Los Angeles. California led other states to sue the Trump administration on Friday over new fuel efficiency standards.

item.title: Powerful Wildfires Require a New Approach, California Report Finds
item.description: A report on the fires that devastated the Los Angeles area in early 2025 recommended that local governments take a broader approach to preparedness and emergency response.
item.dc:creator: Shawn Hubler
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: The clearest lesson from the Palisades and Altadena fires was the extent to which climate-driven fires are outstripping modern firefighting, a new report found.

item.title: He Wrote the Book on the Sedgwick ‘Family Disease,’ and Succumbed to It
item.description: John Sedgwick was born into an illustrious family, but privilege was only part of the story.
item.dc:creator: Penelope Green
item.media:credit: Evan Richman for The New York Times

item.title: Ukraine Reports First Combat Use of Its Own Ballistic Missile
item.description: While the missile fired on Thursday has a limited range, Kyiv is developing a larger weapon that could strike Moscow.
item.dc:creator: Andrew E. Kramer
item.media:description: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine trumpeted the launch of the country’s first domestically made ballistic missile.

item.title: Russia Is Planning Its Most Powerful Blow Yet to Try to Freeze Ukraine
item.description: Ukraine showed European partners what it said were intercepted Russian plans to cut off major cities from power, heat and water this winter.
item.dc:creator: Constant Méheut and Jędrzej Nowicki
item.media:description: Overlooking the Dnipro River before the autumn and winter period in Kyiv, Ukraine.

item.title: Student Protests Rattle France as Police Clashes Bring Blockades and Tear Gas
item.description: Days of unrest have affected more than 1,000 schools across France as high school students push for better standards.
item.dc:creator: Ségolène Le Stradic and Mark Landler
item.media:description: Trying to kick a tear-gas canister during clashes with the police on Thursday in Seine-Saint-Denis, near Paris. Students in about 1,000 French schools are protesting a lack of resources in education.

item.title: Trump Is Getting Desperate. It Shows.

item.title: Missouri Man Discovers Michael McDonald of the Doobie Brothers Is His Biological Father
item.description: Michael Goessling’s first phone call with his biological father brought a shock: He was speaking to Michael McDonald of the Doobie Brothers.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Sinco Kelleher
item.media:description: A man who was adopted as an infant found out his biological father is Grammy Award-winning singer Michael McDonald.
